preamble: The voiceless velar fricative [x] is replaced by the aspirated velar stop [kʰ], a fortition that keeps the voiceless velar place and turns continuous friction into a stop with an aspirated release. It arises where /x/ merges with an existing /kʰ/: in Thai the Sukhothai-era letter ฃ, which spelled a distinct velar fricative, fell together with ข [kʰ]; and across Indo-Aryan, Persian and Arabic loans with /x/ are nativized with /kʰ/, regularly in Bengali, Marathi and Konkani and outside careful speech in Hindi.

examples.from: Sukhothai ฃาย (ฃ = velar fricative) 'to sell'
examples.note: The Ram Khamhaeng inscription writes eleven words with ฃ; later inscriptions confuse ฃ and ข, and all such words are now spelled with ข [kʰ]. Li (1977) reconstructs the series as Proto-Tai *x; Pittayaporn (2009) reconstructs uvular *q, so the value of ฃ before the merger is debated.
Obsolete spelling with ฃ replaced by ข.
Outside careful educated speech the borrowed fricative is replaced by native /kʰ/; the nuqta-less spelling reflects this.
Same substitution; Wiktionary lists both pronunciations.
Bengali has no /x/; Perso-Arabic x is regularly borrowed as kʰ.
From earlier খারাব with final devoicing.
Loanword nativized with the aspirated stop; Marathi खबर is likewise /kʰə.bəɾ/.
